page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor with a clock frequency of 2.55 GHz, provisioning 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is set at 16.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB per core and maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio under a dedicated CPU allocation model.

Hardware provisions do not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, meaning operational deployments require attached network block storage for persistent state. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address for external network routing. By avoiding bundled local NVMe drives and GPU hardware, the instance keeps operational overhead aligned purely with host processor and memory consumption.

The VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-16 offers cost-efficient compute capacity for non-accelerated enterprise software. Its resource distribution makes it well suited for standard application servers, microservices hosting, container clusters, continuous integration workers, and lightweight relational or document databases.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 platform operating at 2.55 GHz. Configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs, it features 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation. The shape includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no integrated local storage, and includes no GPU hardware. Without local non-volatile storage, workloads rely on network-attached block volumes for persistence. This flexible configuration offers an economical balance between processing capability and memory capacity, delivering stable multi-threaded execution for environments that do not require specialized hardware accelerators. It is suitable for application hosting, containerized microservices, development pipelines, continuous integration workloads, and lightweight database management.
